newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul won ends lower in aftermath of intervention.
newsitem.headline: Seoul won ends lower in aftermath of intervention.

text.p: The won closed lower against the dollar on Tuesday as the central bank's dollar buying on Monday depressed sentiment for the local currency, dealers said.
The won closed at 891.10, against Monday's closing of 890.60. It opened at a high of 890.50 and hit a low of 891.30.
"Monday's intervention signalled that the dollar would be supported at above 890 level. Trading was narrowly ranged and will likely be that way for the time being," said a domestic bank dealer.
Dealers said there were some importer settlements, estimated at more than $300 million.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 891.00 on Wednesday, against 890.00 today.
Dealers estimated the central bank's dollar buying on Monday at more than $500 million.
The yen's strength against the dollar limited the won's further fall, they said.
Dealers forecast trading would range from 890.50 to 892.00 on Wednesday.
